title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 17th Congressional District
area: Pittsburgh's northern and western suburbs, including parts of Beaver and Allegheny counties.

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Chris Deluzio ran unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Tony Guy defeated Jesse Vodvarka in the Republican primary, 53.3% to 46.7% (19,581 to 17,183 votes).

candidates.name: Chris Deluzio
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the May 19 Democratic primary

summary.text: Chris Deluzio is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 17th District, first elected in 2022. A Pittsburgh-area native and Naval Academy graduate, he served as a Navy officer, including a deployment in Iraq, and then worked as a voting-rights and election-security attorney and policy director at Pitt Cyber. He serves on the Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1984; according to his official biography, he is a native of Thornburg and attended Bishop Canevin High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Naval Academy in 2006 and a law degree from Georgetown University in 2013; his official biography says the law degree was awarded magna cum laude.
Commissioned as an active-duty surface warfare officer in the U.S. Navy; his service included three deployments, including a tour with U.S. Army Civil Affairs in Iraq.
After law school, clerked for a federal judge (Ballotpedia lists the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York) and worked in private legal practice.

Worked on the Voting Rights and Election Security teams at the Brennan Center for Justice, then as policy director of the University of Pittsburgh Institute for Cyber Law, Policy, and Security (Pitt Cyber).
Was part of the Pitt Faculty Organizing Committee with the United Steelworkers, which won a faculty union at the University of Pittsburgh.

First won public office in 2022, defeating Sean Meloy in the May Democratic primary and Republican Jeremy Shaffer in the November general election; he was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Rob Mercuri.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (Readiness and Seapower and Projection Forces subcommittees) and the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Aviation and Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees); he previously served on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee.
His official biography says he lives with his family in Allegheny County.

priorities.text: Describes himself as a voting rights attorney who worked to protect voting rights and elections before running for Congress.
priorities.quote: As a lawyer, Chris worked to protect voting rights and our elections as the policy director at Pitt Cyber and previously at the Brennan Center for Justice.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Committee on Armed Services for the 2025–2026 term.

candidates.name: Tony Guy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary, defeating Jesse Vodvarka 53.3% to 46.7%

summary.text: Tony Guy is the Republican nominee for Pennsylvania's 17th District and the Beaver County Sheriff. According to his campaign website, he served 26 years with the Pennsylvania State Police before being elected sheriff in 2016. He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Jesse Vodvarka and describes his priorities as law enforcement, border security and economic growth.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a lifelong resident of Beaver County and lives in Hopewell Township with his wife, Sylvia, to whom he has been married for over 35 years; they have a daughter and three grandchildren.

Began his career with the Pennsylvania State Police in 1984 and served 26 years, with assignments in patrol, the motorcycle unit, vice, polygraph and criminal investigations, including the State Police Special Emergency Response Team, per his campaign website.

As a Troop B polygraph examiner he conducted over 1,000 examinations, according to his campaign website; he was later promoted to sergeant and ended his State Police career as supervisor of the Troop B Criminal Investigations Unit.

Elected Beaver County Sheriff in 2016; his campaign website says the office under him adopted merit-based hiring and promotion and earned accreditation from the Pennsylvania Law Enforcement Accreditation Council.
His campaign website says he received the Beaver Valley Chiefs of Police Association Distinguished Service Award in 2023.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the 17th District, defeating Jesse Vodvarka.
